本的起点.en: Dimitri's Restaurant, in the city of Akos, southern Tyche.
AGATA: I am Agata, of the Order of the Phylax.
AGATA: Three days ago, you manifested magical powers for the first time.
AGATA: No, it is possible for anyone to manifest magical powers, at any time.
BEN: My landlord isn't going to care whether I have magic or not.

世界规则.en: AGATA: Our mission is to prevent the use of dangerous magic.
AGATA: But magical powers can emerge in anyone. Sometimes... in the wrong person, in the wrong place.
AGATA: And that is simply the way the world works. The order is our attempt to save what is left of civilization.
KERAUNOS: It is a strange tale. It begins nearly a hundred and fifty years ago...
KERAUNOS: Why should we do anything? Magic is what it is.
HAELAN: His warlike intentions were lamentable, but there is still much we can learn from the way he systematized magic.
HEIZER: Yes! Imagine if the right people had that power!
LE DERNIER: Magic has been the amplifier of human suffering, through all of history.
LE DERNIER: I would rather see a world without magic.
HAELAN: Abandoning magic would be going too far.
HAELAN: Surely it could be studied and regulated, before it comes to something so drastic?
BERNARD: Because the whole world lost their magic.
BERNARD: The wild creatures still have their magic, and now we have very little to fight back with. So, good luck.
KERAUNOS: When we left Mt. Nibaros, Pierre Le Dernier's wish for a world without magic had come true.
KERAUNOS: Not only that. I did not wish for anything. I believed as the wise men of my country believed: that magic was like the wind.
KERAUNOS: You do not know where it comes from, or where it is going. And so a separate world was born.
CORDELIA: Four worlds must have been created. One for each of the sages.
CORDELIA: But the truth must be because Haelan Reed wanted a world where magic could be studied and controlled. That desire created yet another world.
KERAUNOS: In all four worlds, there is one constant. The ancient ruins of Shinar were unaffected by the division of the worlds.
KERAUNOS: The most valuable Shinari relic is a book called the Palimpsest. It resides at the bottom of the Royal Archives, northeast of Seren.
KERAUNOS: If all of us stand beside that book, in three different worlds, I should be able to triangulate our relative positions. Then, I can help you cross over.

会合及口语翻译.en: KERAUNOS: ...but I found only a few notes, scratched out by scholars who were left stranded, after the worlds split.
KERAUNOS: While we are all standing near the Palimpsest, I can accurately assess your positions and allow you to cross between worlds.
BEN: Wait, you understand me!? And I understood you...?
NIKOLAI: Yeah, Zikaron's magic allows everyone to understand each other.
BEN: Oh, man, thank you. Speaking their language is like talking with grapes in your mouth.

成长与选择.en: URALT: Society must be ruled by the best men. Not merely good men in relation to some arbitrary standard, but men of absolute virtue.
URALT: Everything I have set in motion is permissible in the defense of civilization, itself.
ALEXANDRA: What's the point of civilization...
ALEXANDRA: ...if you're only using it to sacrifice more people, faster?
MAIMUN: These are the memories of the people whom Chancellor Uralt has destroyed.
MAIMUN: One of Zikaron's primary purposes is to allow them to formally accuse Uralt of his crimes.
ALEXANDRA: I've got the keys! Everyone get ready!
ALEXANDRA: The copper in the wires.
ALEXANDRA: I can hear it... feel it. I know where it's all going.

牺牲.en: MAIMUN: You must fulfil Zikaron's final function. He brought you here, but he cannot cast the spell.
MAIMUN: Thousands of years ago, my people stole a magic spell from their oppressors, the Shinari.
????: Your friend is very weak. The energy of the spell is the only thing keeping him alive. It won't last much longer.
HAELAN: I'm sorry, Nikolai. I should never have let this happen.
HAELAN: I suspected that, like me, Gustav Heizer must still be alive, after all these years.
HAELAN: My time, and the world that I created, are at an end. You will have to determine what comes next.
HAELAN: But I can still do one last thing.
NIKOLAI: A sergeant's job is to take someone else's big ideas and get them done... with a broken compass, a bad map[oxfordComma /] and half a box of ammo.

记忆与文字.en: SYMON: Tati, what if it's my grandparents who spoke through the memory golem? They went to the temple to commit their memories to him, before the Ausleners came.
DREYFUSS: Yes... there's centuries of memory inside him. Maybe millennia. I can see the encoding spells.
DREYFUSS: To preserve our culture, memory golems were built to think, hide[oxfordComma /] and even fight back.
CORDELIA: I have noticed that Zikaron's translation magic does not work on text.
NIKOLAI: Are you going to extract the memories from Zikaron?
DREYFUSS: Soon, duplicate copies of Zikaron's memories will be stored here, for our people to find.

山顶争论.en: CORDELIA: We must put the world back the way it was, in the beginning.
BEN: Why?
CORDELIA: Because it is the right and natural state of the world. The split brought about a cataclysm, in most places, did it not?
CORDELIA: Almost all of history, all of mankind's journey toward enlightenment, in fact, took place in a unified world. Surely, we want to return everyone to that state?
AGATA: I think I have to agree. Anything would be better than the situation we have in Tyche, right now.
AGATA: If putting the world back the way it was would stop that chaos, then we have to do it.
JEROME: But at what cost?
NIKOLAI: What do you mean?
JEROME: The split between the worlds caused a famine, a war[oxfordComma /] and a series of natural disasters.
JEROME: Who knows what might happen when we reverse it?
NIKOLAI: It's gotta be better than what's happening now, right?
NIKOLAI: I mean, there's a war going on, and if EITHER side wins... it will be a bloodbath. Millions will die. We need other countries there to prevent it.
JEROME: And I will help them, where I am able.
JEROME: But I also swore an oath, as a doctor, to do no harm.
CORDELIA: And you have violated that oath, countless times. Including just a moment ago.
JEROME: That's not the same, and you know it. When someone takes up arms and steps onto a battlefield, they consent to whatever might happen next.
BEN: Can we just hang on, a sec? I'd be afraid to even plan a menu in your country, because you're all so afraid of spices.
BEN: But we're supposed to just decide how the WORLD works, for EVERYBODY? I don't think so.
NIKOLAI: We have to do something. We can't come all this way and take no action.
JUNA: Do we really have to do anything?
JUNA: I know humans suffered a lot from the worlds splitting... but plenty of other people did, too.
JUNA: There were animals that lost their whole food source. Flocks and herds that were split up. Entire species of animals that died in horrible ways.
JUNA: If they were voting with us, right now, things would be way different.
CORDELIA: So... this is a vote?
CORDELIA: Very well, then. Since Zikaron probably lacks the capacity to contribute...
CORDELIA: It comes down to you, dear girl.
ALEXANDRA: Look...
ALEXANDRA: It feels like we've been on this whole quest for a long time. But... not that long ago, I was just trying to run a grocery store.
ALEXANDRA: And now that this is over... I'll probably just go right back there. And that'll be enough for me.
ALEXANDRA: (What am I even trying to say...?)
ALEXANDRA: The dead guy... the chancellor... I met him. I was alone with him. And I only know one thing, for sure.
ALEXANDRA: He made his last speech for a reason. To make us think the way he wanted us to think.
ALEXANDRA: That's what he did for a living. That's the kind of person he was.
ALEXANDRA: I think he wanted us to either keep the worlds split, or join them back together. He would have been happy, either way.
ALEXANDRA: Because either way, he would be the reason why the world changed. And everyone would remember him for it.
CORDELIA: Sadly, those are the two options we are presented with.
BEN: Really?
BEN: If she's right about that bastard... and lemme tell ya, he sounds like most of the bastards I've ever met...
BEN: Then why do we need to do what he wants? Let's stick it to him, instead.
CORDELIA: Incredible insights, as usual.
NIKOLAI: Hang on, he's right.
NIKOLAI: They trained us for this, in the army. The enemy wants to force you into their preferred course of action.
NIKOLAI: But you don't have to take the bait. Coming up with a new strategy that the enemy doesn't expect... that's what you're SUPPOSED to do.
JEROME: Something a bit more down-the-middle?
ALEXANDRA: I don't actually know what that would be, though...
AGATA: I have an idea.

生活尾声.en: ALEXANDRA: (Why is saving the world less complicated than running a shop...?)
MARIE: No, honey. The other fridge.
ALEXANDRA: Yeah, it's pretty much cold all year round, over there. I think the only problem would be if the bears find a way in.
ALEXANDRA: I helped him alter the soil chemistry in his tomato patch.
JUNA: Most of that was just using my nose.
BEN: Niko helped out by fixing my ovens to heat perfectly.
NIKOLAI: That wasn't magic. I just installed better heat sensors and insulation.
JEROME: There may or may not be one olive grove which gets slightly more rain than the rest.
CORDELIA: You may be without peer, in any world that exists.
BEN: How am I supposed to remember him? He never eats anything!
